configuration: PHYSICS=RHD; 2D CARTESIAN; 280x80 zones; solver hll; LINEAR reconstruction; RK2 time stepping; RADIATION=YES; tstop 0.28 (the official deck says 1.5; see graded_window); CFL 0.4; dbl output '1.5 -1 single_file'
variant: ic/variant/pluto.ini multiplies [Parameters] RHO0 by (1 + 1e-15): 1.0e14 becomes 100000000000000.11, one ulp of a value the initial condition is built from (init.c reads g_inputParam[RHO0]). Every initial value that depends on it moves at round-off while the physics is unchanged, so the two runs differ by rounding only and their spread is the floor of this check.
altbuild: the same pinned source and nominal deck built with the Linux.gcc.defs GCC architecture but make CFLAGS='-c -O0' instead of the nominal -O3 compiler flags: an unoptimized build a correct candidate could plausibly use

comparison.files: grid.out (cell edges under the bound), the frame set dbl.out declares (a gate), and the final data.NNNN.dbl frame at t = tstop: every variable, staggered components included, plus its time; intermediate frames are reported, not graded, because PLUTO writes them at the first step past the dump time (Src/main.c, CheckForOutput) and two correct runs do not share that time
comparison.rule: abs(candidate - reference) <= atol + rtol * abs(reference) for every value
comparison.relative_term_basis: the implicit radiation-matter step converges to RADIATION_ERROR = 1e-7 (Src/Radiation/radiation.h:87), a one-ulp difference changes its iteration count, and through the gas-radiation coupling that reaches 1e-4 relative in the gas pressure (density stays at 1e-9, the radiation energy at 2e-7); the relative term is ten times that measured floor, and a wrong Kramers exponent or opacity coefficient changes the radiation energy in the shadow by order one

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck on 2026-09-08: run.sh altbuild (same Linux.gcc.defs GCC architecture with make CFLAGS='-c -O0' instead of its nominal -O3 compiler flags) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py: bit-identical graded output

altbuild.what: same Linux.gcc.defs GCC architecture with make CFLAGS='-c -O0' instead of its nominal -O3 compiler flags

warrant: The graded observable is the state PLUTO writes for this configuration (every variable of the final dbl frame at t = tstop, its time and the grid edges; intermediate frames must exist but are not graded, because PLUTO writes them at the first step past the dump time (Src/main.c, CheckForOutput) so their physical time depends on the step sequence), compared value by value under |candidate - reference| <= 1e-8 + 0.001|reference|: the implicit radiation-matter step converges to RADIATION_ERROR = 1e-7 (Src/Radiation/radiation.h:87), a one-ulp difference changes its iteration count, and through the gas-radiation coupling that reaches 1e-4 relative in the gas pressure (density stays at 1e-9, the radiation energy at 2e-7); the relative term is ten times that measured floor, and a wrong Kramers exponent or opacity coefficient changes the radiation energy in the shadow by order one.  What the check exercises: A free-streaming radiation beam injected from the left hits an opaque ellipse and must cast a sharp shadow behind it (Hayes & Norman 2003) on a 280x80 grid covering the whole ellipse with outflow boundaries. The absorption opacity follows Kramers' law kappa ~ rho T^-3.5 through the user-defined UserDefOpacities hook enabled by RADIATION_VAR_OPACITIES. The bound is physical because a faithful port differs from the reference only by rounding while the nearest real fault lands orders of magnitude above it: a closure that isotropises the flux fills in the shadow; a wrong opacity hook or temperature evaluation changes the heating of the ellipse and the shadow edge. It is achievable because the state is double precision end to end (Src/structs.h:524, the Vc array) and two legitimate runs differ only in the order of floating-point operations; the relative term sits one decade above the 1e-9 branch thresholds where a rounding difference can flip a solver decision (Src/HD/hllc.c:169, Src/MHD/hll.c:161, Src/MHD/eigenv.c:298, the small_p and small_rho floors of Src/HD/two_shock.c:29), and the absolute term is the measured floor of the components that are zero or near zero in these configurations: the calibration runs of 2026-09-02 put round-off noise on such components at 1e-11 to 4e-9 after 1e2 to 1e4 steps (a one-ulp shift of the time-step sequence times the local gradient), so 1e-8 sits a decade above that floor and five orders below any fault, while the relative term still governs every field of order unity. The measured floor of this check is the nominal-versus-variant spread recorded in evidence; where that spread exceeds the bound the policy is revised from the number, never loosened by hand.

graded_window.note: the graded window is set so that the whole suite fits the 900 s budget (the CLI sums per-check time on the declared cores; the official window measured 42 s on the calibration host)
